To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
security metrics for the life cycle are not well developed, and that the most commonly used security metric is the vulnerability count.

(1) 324 unique metrics have been proposed for the software development lifecycle; (2) 85% of these metrics have been proposed by their authors, without external validation; (3) approximately 60% have been validated empirically; (4) 1.5 % of the metrics measure the testing phase; (5) the most used metric is vulnerability count.
the field of security measurement in software development has a small number of metrics that are well validated and used, but the field has yet to converge to an accepted set of security metrics.
